items.title: How Calm-Abiding and Insight Reinforce Each Other

items.zh: 如是依止淨行所緣，尋思六事差別觀已，數數於內令心寂靜，數數復於如所尋思，以勝觀行審諦伺察。彼由奢摩他為依止故，令毘鉢舍那速得清淨；復由毘鉢舍那為依止故，令奢摩他增長廣大。
items.en: Thus, relying on the objects for purifying conduct, having investigated the six-thing differentiated contemplation, one repeatedly settles the mind inwardly into stillness, and then repeatedly, with respect to what has been investigated, carefully and truthfully examines it further through superior insight practice. Relying on calm-abiding, insight swiftly becomes purified; and relying, in turn, on insight, calm-abiding grows and expands.

items.title: Section: Skilful-Means and Purifying-Affliction Objects Deferred — the Fourth Category of Meditation Objects Named

items.zh: 若依止善巧所緣及淨惑所緣，尋思六事差別所緣毘鉢舍那，於其自處我後當說。
items.en: As for investigating insight with objects differentiated by the six things by relying on skilful-means objects or purifying-affliction objects, I shall explain these later, in their own proper place.

items.title: Nine Kinds of Preparatory Practice, Bright and Dark

items.zh: 復次，此中有九種白品所攝加行。與此相違，當知即是九種黑品所攝加行。云何名為白品所攝九種加行？一、相應加行，二、串習加行，三、無倒加行，四、不緩加行，五、應時加行，六、解了加行，七、無厭足加行，八、不捨軛加行，九、正加行。
items.en: Further, herein there are nine kinds of preparatory practice belonging to the bright category. The reverse of these should be known as the nine kinds of preparatory practice belonging to the dark category. What are the nine kinds of preparatory practice belonging to the bright category? First, fitting practice. Second, habituated practice. Third, unslackening practice. Fourth, undistorted practice. Fifth, timely practice. Sixth, understanding practice. Seventh, insatiable practice. Eighth, unabandoning practice. Ninth, correct practice.

items.title: Section: What the Nine Practices Accomplish — Speed to Attainment, Bright and Dark

items.zh: 由此九種白品所攝加行故，能令其心速疾得定，令三摩地轉更勝進。又由此故，於所應往地及隨所應得，速疾能往、能得，無有稽遲。黑品所攝九種加行，不能令心速疾得定，不令三摩地轉更勝進。又由此故，於所應往地及隨所應得，極大稽遲，不能速疾往趣、獲得。
items.en: Through these nine kinds of preparatory practice belonging to the bright category, the mind swiftly attains concentration, and samādhi continues to advance further still. Further, through these, one swiftly reaches and attains whatever stage and whatever level are to be reached, without delay. The nine kinds of preparatory practice belonging to the dark category do not enable the mind to swiftly attain concentration, nor do they enable samādhi to advance further. Further, through these, one is greatly delayed in reaching whatever stage and whatever level are to be reached, unable to swiftly arrive at or attain them.

items.title: Fitting Practice: Matching the Object to One's Own Temperament

items.zh: 云何名為相應加行？謂若貪行者，應於不淨安住其心；若瞋行者，應於慈愍安住其心；若癡行者，應於緣起安住其心；若憍慢行者，應於界差別安住其心；若尋思行者，應於阿那波那念安住其心；若等分行者，或薄塵行者，應隨所樂攀緣一境安住其心；勤修加行。如是名為相應加行。
items.en: What is fitting practice? That is, one dominated by craving should settle the mind on impurity; one dominated by hatred should settle the mind on loving-kindness; one dominated by delusion should settle the mind on dependent origination; one dominated by pride should settle the mind on elemental analysis; one dominated by discursive thought should settle the mind on mindfulness of the in-breath and out-breath; and one whose afflictions are evenly balanced, or lightly present, should settle the mind on whichever object he prefers, diligently cultivating the practice. This is called fitting practice.

items.title: Habituated Practice: Distinguishing the Seasoned Practitioner from the True Beginner

items.zh: 云何名為串習加行？謂於奢摩他、毘鉢舍那，已曾數習乃至少分，非於一切皆初修業。所以者何？初修業者，雖於相應所緣境界勤修加行，而有諸蓋數數現行，身心麁重。由是因緣，不能令心速疾得定。如是名為串習加行。
items.en: What is habituated practice? That is, one who has already repeatedly practised calm-abiding and insight, at least to some degree — not one who is, in every respect, a complete beginner. Why is this? Because a complete beginner, even while diligently applying effort to a fitting object, still has the hindrances repeatedly manifesting, and body and mind remain coarse and heavy. For this reason, the mind cannot swiftly attain concentration. This is called habituated practice.

items.title: Section: Unslackening Practice — Not Delighting in Busywork, Not Delighting in Crowds, Urgent Resolve

items.zh: 云何名為不緩加行？謂無間方便、殷重方便勤修觀行。若從定出，或為乞食，或為恭敬承事師長，或為看病，或為隨順修和敬業，或為所餘如是等類諸所作事；而心於彼所作事業，不全隨順、不全趣向、不全臨入，唯有速疾令事究竟，還復精勤宴坐寂靜、修諸觀行。
items.en: What is unslackening practice? That is, cultivating meditative practice with uninterrupted, earnest effort. If, having risen from concentration, one must beg for alms, attend respectfully upon a teacher, tend the sick, act in accordance with the six kinds of harmony, or carry out other such necessary tasks — the mind, with respect to these tasks, does not fully yield to them, does not fully turn towards them, does not fully enter into them; one merely brings the task swiftly to completion and then returns once more to diligent, still sitting, cultivating meditative practice.

items.zh: 若有苾芻、苾芻尼、鄔波索迦、剎帝利、婆羅門等種種異眾共相會遇，雖久雜處，現相語儀；而不相續安立言論，唯樂遠離勤修觀行。又能如是勇猛精進。謂我於今定當趣證所應證得，不應慢緩。何以故？
items.en: If monks, nuns, laymen, warrior-caste persons, brahmins, or other various different assemblies happen to meet, though remaining together for some time, exchanging courteous greetings, one does not continue on with extended conversation, but delights only in seclusion, diligently cultivating meditative practice. Further, one is thereby able to remain courageously diligent in this way: "I must, at this very time, resolutely reach what is to be realised — I should not be slack or delay."

items.title: The Causes of Sudden Death, and Resolving to Make the Most of Whatever Time Remains

items.zh: 我有多種橫死因緣。所謂身中或風、或熱、或痰發動；或所飲食不正消化，住在身中成宿食病；或為於外蛇蝎、蚰蜒、百足等類諸惡毒蟲之所蛆蠚；或復為人非人類等之所驚恐；因斯夭沒。於如是等諸橫死處恒常思惟，修無常想，住不放逸。
items.en: I have many possible causes of sudden death: perhaps wind, heat, or phlegm disorders arising within the body; or food improperly digested, remaining in the body and becoming a lodged ailment; or being stung or bitten by outer venomous creatures such as snakes, scorpions, centipedes, or the like; or being terrified by humans or non-humans — and dying prematurely through any of these. Constantly reflecting on such causes of sudden death, one cultivates the perception of impermanence, and abides in non-heedlessness.

items.zh: 由住如是不放逸故；恒自思惟：我之壽命儻得更經七日、六日、五日、四日、三日、二日、一日、一時、半時、須臾、或半須臾、或經食頃、或從入息至於出息、或從出息至於入息，乃至存活經爾所時，於佛聖教精勤作意修習瑜伽，齊爾所時，於佛聖教，我當決定多有所作。如是名為不緩加行。
items.en: Abiding in such non-heedlessness, one constantly reflects: "Should my life extend for seven more days, or six, or five … for however much time I have left to live, I must diligently direct my attention to cultivating yogic practice within the Buddha's noble teaching; for that entire span of time, within the Buddha's noble teaching, I am resolved to accomplish a great deal." This is called unslackening practice.

blocks.text: How calm and insight support each other, then the first of nine kinds of good preparatory practice. Today's reading includes a sobering reflection on sudden death.

"One repeatedly settles the mind inwardly into stillness, and then repeatedly examines further through superior wisdom." "Relying on calm, insight swiftly becomes purified; relying on insight, calm grows." Master Cháng Bǎi: in calm the mind is clear like still water.

The six-fold investigation of skilful and affliction-purifying objects "I shall explain later, in their proper place". Venerable Miào Jìng notes that the *Pīxún jì*'s author could not find where it is explained.

Fitting; habituated; unslackening; undistorted; timely; understanding; insatiable; unabandoning; correct. Through these, "the mind swiftly attains concentration". Their opposites are nine dark practices.
Each temperament on its object: craving on impurity, hatred on loving-kindness, delusion on dependent origination, pride on the elements, discursive thought on the breath (Day 225).
One who has practised calm and insight "at least to some degree, not a complete beginner": a beginner's body and mind "remain coarse and heavy".

Continuous, earnest effort. Begging for alms, serving the teacher, caring for the sick: done, but the mind "does not fully turn towards them". Meeting others, one exchanges greetings and returns to solitude.

"I have many possible causes of sudden death: wind, heat, or phlegm disorders; food not digested; snakes, scorpions, centipedes…" So: "should my life extend for seven more days, or six, or five… for however much time I have left, I must practise." Master Cháng Bǎi: this is the perception of impermanence put to work.

quiz.q: Calm and insight support each other. What does Venerable Miào Jìng advise when practice feels unsatisfying?
options: if insight feels off, do calm, and vice versa
quiz.why: "Relying on calm-abiding, insight swiftly becomes purified; and relying, in turn, on insight, calm-abiding grows and expands." Venerable Miào Jìng: when insight practice feels unsatisfying, practice calm; when calm feels unsatisfying, you may practise insight.

quiz.q: The text says "I shall explain later." Do the masters say that later passage can be found?
options: both relay the Pixunji author saying he couldn't find it in the treatise
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the Pixunji's author says he did not see this passage in the Yogācārabhūmi — so it isn't there. Master Cháng Bǎi: the six-thing insight relying on skilful objects — this passage is not to be found. Miào Jìng adds one may refer to fascicle 33.

quiz.q: What does Venerable Miào Jìng say "bright-category preparatory practice" is?
options: methods of effort with merit and no fault — nine of them
quiz.why: "Further, herein there are nine kinds of preparatory practice belonging to the bright category." Venerable Miào Jìng: methods of diligent practice with merit and without fault — there are nine.

quiz.q: The bright practices make the mind "swiftly attain concentration." How does Venerable Miào Jìng describe it?
options: the scattered mind like a wild horse quickly settles — from desire-realm to access concentration
quiz.why: "Through these nine kinds of bright practice, the mind swiftly attains concentration, and samādhi continues to advance further." Venerable Miào Jìng: your scattered mind, like a wild horse, quickly attains concentration — from desire-realm concentration to access concentration.

quiz.q: Fitting practice matches the object to one's temperament. How do the masters stress this?
options: Miào Jìng: take the medicine for your illness; Cháng Bǎi: years of breath-counting stalled, switching to elements settled quickly
quiz.why: "One dominated by pride should settle the mind on elemental analysis; one dominated by discursive thought, on breath mindfulness." Venerable Miào Jìng: you have this illness, so take this medicine — when it fits, success comes easily. Master Cháng Bǎi: someone practised breath-counting for years with little change, then switched to elemental analysis and quickly calmed down.

quiz.q: Habituated practice includes "even a small portion." Does having only the mark-learning engagement count?
options: Miào Jìng: mark-learning is the "small portion," so it counts; Cháng Bǎi says it does not
quiz.why: "One who has already repeatedly practised calm-abiding and insight, at least to some degree — not one who is, in every respect, a complete beginner." Venerable Miào Jìng, citing the Pixunji: "having only practised mark-learning engagement is called a small portion." Master Cháng Bǎi: having only reached mark-learning engagement by repetition does not count as habituated practice. By the text's "even a small portion," it should be included.

quiz.q: "I have many causes of sudden death." How does Master Cháng Bǎi define 橫死?
options: not dying of old age, but dying when one shouldn't
quiz.why: "I have many possible causes of sudden death: perhaps wind, heat, or phlegm disorders arising within the body." Master Cháng Bǎi: sudden death is not dying peacefully at life's end, but dying when one should not.
